newsitem.title: JORDAN: Mubarak arrives in Jordan for Mideast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak arrives in Jordan for Mideast peace talks.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak arrived in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba on Saturday for talks with King Hussein on the deadlock in Israeli-PLO peacemaking, officials said on Saturday.
Witnesses said King Hussein welcomed Mubarak at Aqaba airport and drove him to his seaside palace for the one-day meeting.
Palestinian-Israeli peace talks have been deadlocked since March when Israel began building a controversial Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel since 1967.
The Palestinians say talks can resume only after Israel stops work on the settlement. Egypt, which considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the peace talks, supports their position.

Mubarak's talks are in advance of a meeting with Netanyahu on Tuesday at the Egyptian Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh. Egypt, partner to a 1979 treaty with Israel, hopes to break the Israel-PLO deadlock.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks with Mubarak on Wednesday and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in remarks broadcast on Friday the Mubarak-Netanyahu summit would succeed if Israel agreed to stop the building.
Both Egypt and Jordan have peace treaties with Israel but ties between Amman and the Jewish state are much stronger than those linking Cairo and Israel.
